answer: Per-identity proof-of-work throttling resists Sybil keys. Each new wallet must burn compute to find a nonce under a target that tightens as network hashrate grows, so mass-registering a thousand aliases costs about a thousand times the energy and hardware time of one real miner. Payouts track work, not key count, so splitting hashrate adds no multiplier, and a falcon-fast flood of fresh keys is itself a clear statistical signal operators can flag. Every fake canyon of identities must be paid for in electricity.
